newsitem.title: UK: Stg/mark clings to earlier gains, holds above 2.76.
newsitem.headline: Stg/mark clings to earlier gains, holds above 2.76.

text.p: 1440 GMT - Sterling clung on to most gains above 2.76 marks in late Europe after rocketing up over one pfennig after BoE called for fresh rise in interest rates in coming months.

* Sterling/mark at 2.7645/50, just off highs at 2.7723, vs 2.7510/20 ahead of the report and 2.7655/65 in late Europe on Monday. Cable firmer at $1.6308/13 after drop in U.S. retail sales, was at $1.6202/12 ahead of BoE report.

* The BoE's quarterly inflation report, the first since the Bank was granted freedom by UK Chancellor Gordon Brown to set interest rates, said stg strength should push RPIX well below 2.5 percent this year.
* The BoE said sterling is hurting output, exports less than expected in February but also that higher rates could worsen economic imbalance.

Sterling jumped more than one pfennig and half a cent in Europe after the Bank of England called for a fresh rise in interest rates and warned inflation was likely to overshoot without more policy action. "The surprise is that they are still calling for another tightening of policy before seeing the effects of the last one," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. Only last week rates were hiked to 6.25 percent from 6.0 percent in a bid to keep inflation in check. But in its first report since it was granted the freedom to set rates, the BoE warned inflation was likely to overshoot without policy action. At 1325 GMT sterling/mark was trading at 2.7645/50 marks against 2.7510/20 ahead of the BoE report and 2.7655/65 in late Europe on Monday. Against the dollar, sterling stood at $1.6302/12 against $1.6202/12 and $1.6230/40.
The BoE, in its quarterly inflation report, said a further tightening was needed in monetary policy if the inflation target of 2.5 percent or lower would be hit in the medium-term.

"The central projection for inflation and the risks surrounding it suggests that, on the present evidence, there is still likely to be a need for some further moderate tightening policy in the months ahead," it said.
At a press briefing on the report, chief economist Mervyn King said the Bank would have to "seriously consider raising interest rates in the coming months."
But interest rate decisions could not be second-guessed, even on the basis of the report, King said.
Last week's rise in rates "has clearly lowered the expectations (on inflation), all things being equal", he added.

In the report, the Bank said the short-term outlook for inflation was encouraging because of the strength of sterling, but this was likely to be a one-off shock to the price level. The Bank's chief economist added the pound would help push inflation "well below 2.5 percent later this year. But that is not an adequate response to meeting the target two years or so ahead".
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown has adopted his predecessor's medium-term target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation.

"The BoE is basically saying not enough has been done, more needs to be done...higher rates are necessary," said James Barty, U.K. economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "The only thing that will stop higher rates is if the Chancellor goes down the route of significant tax increases," said Barty.
Barty, however, said he expects rates to hit around 7.0 percent by year-end.

"This economy has got a lot of momentum behind it...We will see stronger growth in the world economy and my guess is that the peak in rates is probably at least around 7.50 percent," he said. --London newsroom +4471 542 6701
